name: בַּעַלְיָה
summary: A Benjamite, one of Saul's kinsmen who came to David at Ziklag, mighty men who could shoot and sling with right hand or left (1Ch 12:1–2, 6). The name joins בַּעַל “lord” with יָה, the short form of Yahweh: “Yah is lord”, or “lord is Yah”, a name from the days when בַּעַל could still be said of Yahweh (Hos 2:18).

evidence.note: “Eluzai, Jerimoth, וּבְעַלְיָה, Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite.”
The men who came to David at Ziklag, “of Saul's brothers, of Benjamin”.
“Your husband (בֹעֲלַיִךְ) is your Maker, Yahweh of armies is his name”: the root said of Yahweh.

note: TIPNR's Bealiah@1Ch.12.5 is 1Ch 12:6 in the Hebrew numbering. Whether בַּעַל is predicate (“Yah is lord”) or subject (“the lord is Yah”) the form does not say.
